summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 2.4/807)

data.turoyo: <...> Məftakrina, mṣaybarlan hanək kulle, məstaḥmelan i taʕaddayiye kula w uʕdo b raḥa na, mahzamlan w aṯina.
data.translation: <...> We think: we endured all those things, we bore all the persecution, and now that we are at ease, we have fled and come.

rationale: First II.1 Preterit example; overt bare adversity object and parallel endurance predicate. English is supplied project machine translation.

summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 3.17/296)

data.turoyo: <...> W hiye, qašo ʕAziz, mṣaybarle tmonaḥṣar əšne w maksable foṯo gliṯo w dostaniye ġalabe w ḥubo.
data.translation: <...> And he, Father Aziz, endured eighteen years and gained an open face and much friendship and love.

rationale: Third Preterit example; third-person L-agent and explicit duration distinguish it from adversities as objects. English is supplied project machine translation.

Jan supplies overt adversities as direct objects, especially hanək kulle and fronted am mədonani kulle resumed in mṣaybərilan. This clarifies transitive endurance in addition to intransitive patience.

summary: Jan Beṯ-Şawoce has no edition translation. English accompanying the added examples is the supplied project machine translation, copied and cut without retranslation; lexical decisions rest on the Turoyo.
Permitted lookups show ṣbr I/II and sybr I alongside ṣybr II. sybr has very similar msayballe/msaybər with endurance imperatives, while ṣbr II lacks the y-bearing shape.
The glossary's inherited II label is retained for ṣybr despite the different I filing under sybr. Jan's emphatic spelling is copied without merging entries or changing etymologies.
mṣaybərilan may index a plural patient before first-person plural L-agent; the fronted am mədonani kulle supports the patient reference, but segmentation remains a question.
No light-verb construction is evidenced: mṣaybarlan itself carries endurance, with adjacent mdayanlan and məstaḥmelan as separate predicates.
Should sybr I and ṣybr II be cross-indexed as phonetic and stem-label variants? Compare their paradigms before consolidation.
Jan 2.17/3616: confirm mṣaybər-i-lan plural patient plus first-person plural agent, rather than a stem-vowel variant.
Adversities and persecution appear as objects; tmonaḥṣar əšne is a duration rather than a patient. The gloss is widened to state the endurance meaning explicitly.
